item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q014_paper_example_reclassification_pa1492","answer":"In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 from PDB 1t1j and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from PDB 1f8y were treated as more remote structural analogs: PA1492 was placed in its own PA1492-like fold/superfamily rather than in the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase group. The later SCOP reclassification described by Andreeva et al. moved the PA1492 domains into the Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase-like fold at the same superfamily level as 1f8y. In current SCOPe terms, d1t1ja_ is still a separate PA1492 family, while d1f8y chains are in the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase family, but those families now sit in the same Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase-like superfamily/fold. Thus the change was a recognition of probable homology at superfamily strength, not a merger into one family and not enough evidence by itself to transfer the exact 1f8y enzymatic function, active-site annotation, or a close-homology modeling template relationship to PA1492.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
